title: Starting — Air Starter Motor — Installation of the Compensating Duct Clamp and Heat Shield Tab
abstract: Installation of a compensating starter duct clamp and a heat shield tab, for operators using the extended dry motoring cycle daily, where the joint runs hot enough for the original clamp to take a permanent set.

sections.planning_reason: The extended dry motoring cycle adopted for engine core conditioning runs the starter for up to ninety seconds against a previous maximum of thirty. Operators using the longer cycle daily report starter duct joint leakage at five times the fleet rate, and removed clamps show permanent set consistent with a soak temperature well above the qualification figure. Leakage at that joint blows onto the pylon lower fairing and had produced eleven fairing skin heat damage findings by the end of 2023. Aircraft that are not modified will continue to generate both the leak and the fairing finding.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin replaces the starter duct clamp with an item that has a stainless band and a compensating spring section, and adds a formed heat shield tab on the starter tube assembly that protects the clamp from direct radiation off the duct elbow. The tab is secured with titanium bolts into existing bosses. No pipework is cut and no bracket is drilled.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Make sure that the engine is cool and that the bleed system is depressurised. Open the fan cowl to reach zones 462 and 421. Remove the start valve nozzle at FIN 2520ES and renew its seal. Remove the existing starter duct clamp. Install the heat shield tab on the tube assembly D8010116441198 with the bolts EN290030-3C and torque them to the value in the instructions. Install the clamp PE187919-09 over the joint and set the band load with the calibrated tool. Check the clearance between the tab and the heat shield at FIN 293ES. Install the start valve nozzle. Do a starter duct leak check at operating pressure. Do a dry motoring run of the full extended duration and re-check the joint for leakage following task AMM-Z-80-10-11-400-036-A.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable per engine to ZEPHYR-22 and ZEPHYR-24 Evo model aircraft delivered before the production cut-in. Operators who do not use the extended dry motoring cycle may defer embodiment, but the clamp is interchangeable and there is no penalty in fitting it.
sections.material_note: Kit K8010-1003-01 covers one engine and contains the clamp, the heat shield tab, the bolt set and the nozzle seal. Two kits are required per aircraft. All items are short-lead and the calibrated band load tool is available on loan.

type_data.compliance_time: Within 24 months after the date of this Service Bulletin for operators using the extended dry motoring cycle; otherwise at the operator's convenience.
